title: Second year after the estimate rises

company.company_business: IT implementation and managed services for mid-size Indian businesses

narrative_template:
Kalmira's fixed-price contract with {customer} is for ₹{price}. At 31 March 2025 total cost was expected to be ₹{last_year_total_cost} and costs incurred were ₹{costs_last_year}. At 31 March 2026 the estimate is ₹{total_cost} and costs incurred to date are ₹{costs_to_date}. How much revenue does Kalmira recognise in FY 2025-26?

Round amounts to the nearest rupee and percentages to one decimal place. All names are fictional.

rubric.text: Cumulative catch-up with the revised estimate, less last year's revenue.

answer_exprs.revenue_this_year: price * costs_to_date / total_cost - price * costs_last_year / last_year_total_cost

explanation: Cumulative revenue now uses the latest estimate; subtract last year's revenue, which used last year's estimate. Revenue this year = ₹{revenue_this_year}.

mistakes.feedback: You applied the new estimate only to this year's costs. Recompute cumulative revenue with the latest estimate and subtract what was recognised last year; the effect of the change falls in this year (para 43).
That is cumulative revenue. Subtract the revenue recognised last year, on last year's estimate.
